reverse_outline.summary: Three takeaways: approval is built in layers around the bank's decision; provider and merchant both shape it; approval rates only compare under equal setups
Opening example: the same card at one studio travels through two different providers, and two differently licensed senders, depending on online versus counter
What the previous part omitted and this part's focus: the provider's side of the authorization message
The six layers surrounding the issuer's decision, listed, with their effect on approval and reversibility, and a pointer to the figure that draws them
Layers are split between provider and merchant, so approval is co-produced / approval rates describe a setup and should not be compared without aligning conditions
Limits of the evidence: the claim relies on what the two providers publish, with named gaps and unaudited figures
Roadmap: why the six chapters follow the order of constraint, and the question each one asks
Chapter 1 preview: licensed acquirer of record, how the two providers are licensed, and the fictional platform's four arrangements
Chapter 2 preview: non-card methods share an API but differ in what success guarantees, with the direct-debit mistake as case
Chapter 3 preview: a payment as a long-lived record with explicit states, how each provider exposes it, and the delayed set-up case
Chapter 4 preview: why genuine payments are declined, what providers do inside the call, and how a rate gap shrinks under like-for-like counting
Chapter 5 preview: when a second provider helps, what a routing layer does not unify, and the platform's decision not to buy orchestration
Chapter 6 preview: card-present payments, the terminal and offline risk borne by the merchant, and cross-channel unity as three separate properties
What the part enables (locating a problem in one layer; rereading the opening example as two stacks) and where to start reading

results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 13 outline summaries match the controlling ideas of p01 to p13 in the spec's order; the KEY POINTS callout matches no paragraph and restates the thesis statement as the spec places it.

Introduction ¶4, the one unit marked two_ideas, holds one idea with its consequence: the layers have two holders, so an approval is co-produced and a rate describes a setup. This is p04's controlling idea as specified.
Introduction ¶1 to ¶6 set up and state the part claim; the six chapter paragraphs each introduce one of P2-1 to P2-6 in order; the conclusion applies the claim.

Both figures have a caption saying what they show and are introduced in the prose; each Larkfield case and each Stripe/Adyen fact that the draft uses is tied to the point it supports in the same or the next sentence. Note: the draft leaves out some spec evidence (the 700 US studios, the 3.8% and 6% uplift figures, the 115,000-payment arithmetic, the Cologne offline request); none is left unexplained.

All twelve declared transitions are expressed at their boundaries and pick up the declared known information (e.g. 'Those two routes are what Part I left out', 'Seen from that side', 'The layers also have two holders', 'turns from the card networks, which answer in seconds', 'takes up the state machine's failed attempt', 'leaves the payment made at a distance', 'Together the chapters'). The p05 contrast is carried by 'and the record has edges' and a later 'But'; its opening referent is ruled on under flow_is_followable.

results.quote: Figure 2 draws them reversed, device (the terminal) first, as a request crosses them, under shorter labels.
results.finding: Both flow readers re-read this sentence and had to map the six layers just listed to the figure by hand: the figure gives them in the opposite order and under other names than the prose.

results.quote: That claim rests on what Stripe and Adyen publish, and the record has edges.
results.finding: Both flow readers could not tell which claim 'That claim' is, because the sentence before it is the author's own rule and the one before that holds two claims; both also had to decode 'the record has edges'.

results.quote: That claim rests on what Stripe and Adyen publish
results.finding: Both flow readers said the evidence-limits paragraph interrupts the run from the two holders to the chapter order, both proposed moving it to the end of the introduction or under 'Sources and Evidence', and both could not tell why evidence is discussed in two places. The position is the one the spec's flow rationale declares, so the difficulty comes from the order.
results.corroborated_by: second flow reader, section 4 item 1 (and section 2 item 4)

results.quote: the state model holds their instant and late answers
results.finding: Both flow readers report that 'their instant and late answers' relies on something not yet said: that some methods answer late is first stated in the chapter list below.

results.quote: only then can optimization, routing and the terminal be explained
results.finding: Both flow readers report that 'routing' (and for one of them 'optimization') appears here as a layer name for the first time in the running text; the layers paragraph called it 'the choice among providers' and Figure 2 'Providers', so they had to check the names referred to the same layers.

results.quote: so results and webhooks are assembled
results.finding: Both flow readers found the clause vague: it does not say who assembles the results and webhooks or into what, and one had to infer that the merchant builds the payment's record from them.

results.quote: shrink from a 13.5-point gap to 0.8 points at the first attempt once both are counted the same way
results.finding: Both flow readers re-read the sentence: its subject is the rates but what shrinks is the gap, and 'at the first attempt' can attach to the 0.8 points or to the way of counting.

results.quote: one of the 1,140 studios split between the two providers
results.finding: Both flow readers could not tell whether 'split between the two providers' describes the studios or the refund, and read it as conflicting with the opening, where each of these studios uses Stripe online and Adyen at the desk.

results.quote: the acquirer, the method mix, the metric and its denominator are held equal
results.finding: Both flow readers noticed that the KEY POINTS list four things to hold equal and the body lists three ('the acquirer, the method mix and the metric'); 'denominator' appears only in the callout and one reader looked for it in the body and did not find it. The AC-1 reader noted the same mismatch.

Every term on does_not_know that the draft uses is glossed or only named as the spec allows (scheme: 'its body of rules'; acquirer of record explained in its sentence; orchestration only named); issuer, acquirer, authorization, webhook and Keel are on already_knows. Readers noted iDEAL, SEPA direct debit, EEA and K8 as unglossed, but each sentence states the one property it needs and both readers got the point, so these are not material.
The introduction opens on a specific case, states a disputable claim and gives a roadmap; none of the listed weak patterns.
The conclusion is one paragraph that says what the chapters add up to, returns to the opening and names the first chapter; no new idea, no rephrased thesis alone, no body evidence.

'Together the chapters let you place a decline, a late outcome or a provider question in one layer before you change anything' gives the synthesis and the so-what, which no single chapter paragraph states.
'the two routes of the opening card read as two stacks of the same six layers' returns to the p01 case as callback.how declares.

The AC-1 reader states that a 'yes' is not a verdict the network hands back but an outcome produced in six layers around the issuer's decision, and names the six chapters in the expected order (acquiring and licenses, non-card methods, state machine, declines and optimization, routing, in-person). The introduction-only reader predicted the same six subjects in order, the documentary evidence with stated gaps, and the tone.

The first paragraph opens with 1,140 studios in the Netherlands and Germany on Larkfield, charged through Stripe online and Adyen at the front desk; the scenario ledger gives the same figure, countries and split (line 32).
